field.label: Record in the background
field.help: Keep recording threats while the map is closed, as long as the widget is on a dashboard.

field.label: Use external public IP discovery
field.help: Find this firewall's public IPv4 address with an external service (api.ipify.org) when its WAN interface has only a private address, as behind an upstream NAT router. The discovered address is then geolocated with the configured geolocation service, like a public WAN address. Not used when the WAN has a public address or while both coordinates are set.

field.label: Latitude
field.help: Manually override the automatically determined firewall latitude, in signed decimal degrees (for example 40.7128). Set together with Longitude; leave both empty to locate the firewall from its public IP.

field.label: Longitude
field.help: Manually override the automatically determined firewall longitude, in signed decimal degrees (for example -74.0060). Set together with Latitude; leave both empty to locate the firewall from its public IP.

field.label: On a CARP backup
field.help: A CARP backup holds copies of the master's connections (pfsync) without their traffic counters. Mirror shows them, marked as mirrored and ranked by connections and security evidence, so the map is ready when this firewall takes over; Show only this firewall's traffic leaves them out. On the master, or without CARP, this changes nothing.

field.label: Maximum flows on the map
field.help: How many flows the collector ranks and sends to the map each sample, from 25 to 1000. Higher values show more flows but take more processing time and memory. This does not limit firewall states or connections.

field.label: Shortest refresh interval (s)
field.help: How often an open map is refreshed at most. The collector measures what each sample costs and, on a busy firewall, asks for a longer interval so it stays a small share of the CPU; the interval never goes below this.

field.label: Longest refresh interval (s)
field.help: The longest the collector may stretch the interval to, however costly a sample is.

field.label: Memory budget (MiB)
field.help: The most memory the state collector may use per sample. It also sets the largest PF state table the map will process: above it a sample is refused and the map says so, instead of slowing the firewall. Leave empty for 5% of physical memory, at most 1024 MiB. The Status page shows the resulting state limit.

field.label: Country blocklists
field.help: GeoIP aliases (Firewall: Aliases) whose countries the map shows beside each remote's geolocation, as the firewall itself classifies it; the two may disagree. Selecting an alias here blocks nothing and never marks traffic as a threat: blocking stays with your firewall rules.

field.label: Operational sets
field.help: PF tables with a meaning of your own (partners, cloud providers, monitoring...). The map shows which ones contain a remote; they never mark traffic as a threat. Threat lists, Country blocklists and Operational sets together use at most 64 tables.

field.label: Log administrator actions
field.help: Adds to the Firewall Map log who investigated an address (which sends it to RDAP, RIPEstat and AbuseIPDB), changed or deleted threat entries, and saved, annotated or deleted snapshots. Downloads, errors and the collector are always logged.

field.label: Geolocation service
field.help: Where the map looks up the location and network of each address. Downloads go only to the chosen provider; addresses are never sent anywhere.

field.label: MaxMind license key
field.help: Leave empty to keep the stored key. Without a key here, the key of a MaxMind GeoIP alias is used when one exists.

field.label: Remove the stored key
field.help: Deletes the MaxMind key saved here when you save. A key in a MaxMind GeoIP alias is not affected.

field.label: Update every (days)
field.help: How old the database may get before a new one is downloaded.

field.label: Threat lists
field.help: PF tables used to flag traffic on the map and in threat history. With none selected: feed tables and the aliases your block rules use. A curated feed counts only through its FWMAP_* alias (Maintain blocklist aliases).

field.label: AbuseIPDB API key
field.help: Optional: enables abuse reports when investigating an address, and the AbuseIPDB blacklist. Leave empty to keep the stored key.

field.label: Remove the stored key
field.help: Deletes the AbuseIPDB key when you save. Abuse reports and the blacklist stop until a new key is entered.

field.label: Maintain blocklist aliases
field.help: Keeps an FWMAP_* alias for each selected feed and for the AbuseIPDB blacklist. The map flags traffic with these PF tables, so selected feeds and the blacklist need it; you can also use the aliases in your own rules. No rules are added.
